items.title: The base change of an integral ring map along a fibre product is integral
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the fibre product situation integrality of one structure map implies integrality of the corresponding base changed map, and the proof is a 9-line elementwise argument using the identification of the two kernels. It takes an element of the base changed ring, writes down the monic polynomial with coefficients in the source that it satisfies thanks to integrality, lifts the coefficients along the surjection from the fibre product of rings, and then observes that the polynomial relation holds modulo the common kernel; because the two kernels coincide, the last coefficient can be adjusted to make the relation an honest equation, which is the integrality statement. The lift of the coefficients and the kernel adjustment are the two steps, and both are displayed.
